To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the mean squared error (MSE) of the ML and restricted ML estimators of the means of small areas is smaller than the MSE of the corresponding empirical best linear unbiased predictor (EBLUP) of the means; (2) the MSE of the ML estimator is smaller than the one of the restricted ML estimator; (3) the MSE of both estimators is larger for small areas with large sampling errors; (4) the MSE of estimators is smaller in the case

(i) the approximation for the mean squared errors of the ML and restricted ML estimators is accurate; (ii) the approximation for cross-product errors is accurate only when the sample sizes are large; and (iii) the restricted ML estimators perform better than the ML estimators in terms of both mean-squared and mean cross-product errors.
(a) The ML estimator of the covariance matrix of the sampling errors is biased, and (b) the restricted ML estimator is biased, too, but to a lesser extent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of the mean-squared errors of the small area estimators, and with the study of their behaviour when different estimation methods and different model structures are considered.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, when the sample is small or the number of areas is large, the use of ML estimators of the model parameters is recommended, and that the cross-products of the errors should be taken into account in the estimation procedure.
, in general, ML estimators have better performance than restricted ML estimators.

the restricted ML estimator is more efficient than the ML estimator, and that the efficiency of both estimators is higher for the means of the characteristics of small areas with a high number of sampled units.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a unit level model is a useful tool for the construction of small-area estimations in a multivariate framework.
, for small area estimation, ML and restricted ML estimators of parameters are not equivalent.
the ML estimator of the mean-squared errors performs well when the number of areas is large, whereas the restricted ML estimator performs well for small areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given design, the ML estimators of the model parameters perform better than the restricted ML estimators.
, for small areas, the ML estimator is preferable to the REML one, even when the latter is unbiased.
, when the model parameters are estimated by ML, the mean-squared errors of the small-area estimators are not affected by the correlation among the sampling errors.
